response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to analyze the new `ClientPermissionsV2` implementation and the schema changes for correctness, completeness, and consistency with the existing V1 implementation.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java",
      "line": 304,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getResourceName does not handle the new CLIENTS resource type",
      "body": "getResourceName was extended to add a CLIENTS resource type and scopes, but the existing getResourceName() method only resolves resource names for the USERS resource type. For policies with resourceType \"Clients\", the method falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which for schema-created resources is null (display name is never set in getOrCreateResource). For individual client resources whose name is the client UUID, this returns an unhelpful UUID rather than the clientId/username-style identifier. The method should be extended with an `else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType))` branch that handles `resource.getName().equals(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (returning \"All clients\") and resolves individual clients via session.clients().getClientById(realm, resource.getName()), analogous to the USERS handling."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 217,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Potential NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist",
      "body": "In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when resourceStore.findByName returns null the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That helper returns null if no resource of that name exists in the store. The result is passed unconditionally to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), which will throw NullPointerException on `resource`. A null check is needed before calling findByResource. While init() always creates the all-clients resource in a fresh realm, this is a robustness hole for realms where the admin-permissions client exists without the schema resource (e.g., migration edge cases)."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 51,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "style",
      "title": "Dead code: unused Logger field, TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and getEvaluationContext helper",
      "body": "The class declares `private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);` (with the corresponding org.jboss.logging.Logger import) but never references logger. It also imports `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` without using it. The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (lines 262-272) is defined but never invoked anywhere in this class. These should be removed to keep the new file clean."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "requireView() JavaDoc says \"Returns true\" for a void method",
      "body": "The JavaDoc added by this PR for `void requireView();` reads `Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.` Since the method is void and explicitly named `require*`, the doc should describe the exception it throws, e.g., `Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false.` The same issue affects `requireList()` and `requireListClientScopes()`, which were re-documented in this PR but copy the correct pattern, so they read correctly. Only `requireView()` was mis-described."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java",
      "line": 0,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No test coverage for the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope",
      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope, ClientPermissionsV2 implements canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) using it, and the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface documents it. However, PermissionClientTest does not exercise this scope or canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) at all (it covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE together in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but never MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). A test similar to testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but verifying client-scope role mapping with MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, should be added so that the scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) implementation have real coverage."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 138,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getClientsWithPermission includes the literal string \"Clients\" as if it were a client id",
      "body": "`resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` returns every resource whose type is \"Clients\", which includes both per-client resources (whose names are client UUIDs) AND the aggregate all-clients resource whose name is literally the string \"Clients\". When the caller has permission via the all-clients resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and `granted.add(resource.getName())` puts \"Clients\" into the returned set. Callers treat the result as a set of client ids and will try to resolve \"Clients\" as a client, which is not a valid client id. The aggregate resource must be skipped (e.g., by checking `resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and continuing), or callers must be told separately that \"all clients\" permission applies."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 86,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "canView() is inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) regarding MANAGE permission",
      "body": "`canView()` only checks VIEW via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`, but `canView(ClientScopeModel)` checks BOTH VIEW and MANAGE via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. A user with only MANAGE permission on all clients can pass canView(ClientScopeModel) but fails canView(). This asymmetry is inconsistent within the same class and may break listing/filtering paths that consult canView() without per-client evaluation, contradicting the V2 contract that MANAGE implies VIEW. canView() should also accept MANAGE permission, matching the canView(ClientScopeModel) behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "canManageClientScopes() ignores per-client MANAGE permission",
      "body": "`canManageClientScopes()` and `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` only consult `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` against the all-clients resource, never the per-client resource. In testManageOnlyOneClient a user is granted MANAGE only on a specific client and is then expected to be able to removeDefaultClientScope on that same client; this only works if the admin endpoint happens to call canManage(client) instead of canManage(clientScope). Any caller that does consult canManage(ClientScopeModel) for a scope attached to a single specific client will incorrectly deny the operation even when the user clearly manages that client. canManage(ClientScopeModel) should accept a ClientModel context (or canManageClientScopes should also be parameterized) so the per-client permission is honored."
    }
  ]
}
```

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName was extended to add a CLIENTS resource type and scopes, but the existing getResourceName() method only resolves resource names for the USERS resource type. For policies with resourceType "Clients", the method falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which for schema-created resources is null (display name is never set in getOrCreateResource). For individual client resources whose name is the client UUID, this returns an unhelpful UUID rather than the clientId/username-style identifier. The method should be extended with an `else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType))` branch that handles `resource.getName().equals(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (returning "All clients") and resolves individual clients via session.clients().getClientById(realm, resource.getName()), analogous to the USERS handling.

findings.title: Potential NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when resourceStore.findByName returns null the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That helper returns null if no resource of that name exists in the store. The result is passed unconditionally to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), which will throw NullPointerException on `resource`. A null check is needed before calling findByResource. While init() always creates the all-clients resource in a fresh realm, this is a robustness hole for realms where the admin-permissions client exists without the schema resource (e.g., migration edge cases).

findings.title: Dead code: unused Logger field, TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and getEvaluationContext helper
findings.body: The class declares `private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);` (with the corresponding org.jboss.logging.Logger import) but never references logger. It also imports `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` without using it. The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (lines 262-272) is defined but never invoked anywhere in this class. These should be removed to keep the new file clean.

findings.title: requireView() JavaDoc says "Returns true" for a void method
findings.body: The JavaDoc added by this PR for `void requireView();` reads `Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.` Since the method is void and explicitly named `require*`, the doc should describe the exception it throws, e.g., `Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false.` The same issue affects `requireList()` and `requireListClientScopes()`, which were re-documented in this PR but copy the correct pattern, so they read correctly. Only `requireView()` was mis-described.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope, ClientPermissionsV2 implements canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) using it, and the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface documents it. However, PermissionClientTest does not exercise this scope or canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) at all (it covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE together in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but never MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). A test similar to testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but verifying client-scope role mapping with MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, should be added so that the scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) implementation have real coverage.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the literal string "Clients" as if it were a client id
findings.body: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` returns every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes both per-client resources (whose names are client UUIDs) AND the aggregate all-clients resource whose name is literally the string "Clients". When the caller has permission via the all-clients resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and `granted.add(resource.getName())` puts "Clients" into the returned set. Callers treat the result as a set of client ids and will try to resolve "Clients" as a client, which is not a valid client id. The aggregate resource must be skipped (e.g., by checking `resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and continuing), or callers must be told separately that "all clients" permission applies.

findings.title: canView() is inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) regarding MANAGE permission
findings.body: `canView()` only checks VIEW via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`, but `canView(ClientScopeModel)` checks BOTH VIEW and MANAGE via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. A user with only MANAGE permission on all clients can pass canView(ClientScopeModel) but fails canView(). This asymmetry is inconsistent within the same class and may break listing/filtering paths that consult canView() without per-client evaluation, contradicting the V2 contract that MANAGE implies VIEW. canView() should also accept MANAGE permission, matching the canView(ClientScopeModel) behavior.

findings.title: canManageClientScopes() ignores per-client MANAGE permission
findings.body: `canManageClientScopes()` and `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` only consult `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` against the all-clients resource, never the per-client resource. In testManageOnlyOneClient a user is granted MANAGE only on a specific client and is then expected to be able to removeDefaultClientScope on that same client; this only works if the admin endpoint happens to call canManage(client) instead of canManage(clientScope). Any caller that does consult canManage(ClientScopeModel) for a scope attached to a single specific client will incorrectly deny the operation even when the user clearly manages that client. canManage(ClientScopeModel) should accept a ClientModel context (or canManageClientScopes should also be parameterized) so the per-client permission is honored.
